gloss: to fascinate; to captivate; to enchant

definitions.gloss: to fascinate; to captivate; to enchant
definitions.explanation: To charm or captivate an audience through an impressive performance, beauty, or skill. Written with {魅|み} (charm/bewitch) to distinguish it from the ordinary {見|み}せる (to show).

examples.japanese: {観客|かんきゃく}を{魅|み}せた。
{圧倒的|あっとうてき}な{演技|えんぎ}で{人|ひと}々を{魅|み}せる{俳優|はいゆう}だ。
examples.english: He's an actor who captivates people with overwhelming performances.

examples.japanese: そのダンサーは{独自|どくじ}のスタイルで{世界中|せかいじゅう}の{人|ひと}を{魅|み}せ、{一躍|いちやく}スターになった。
examples.english: The dancer captivated people around the world with a unique style and became a star overnight.

notes:
An ichidan verb using the kanji {魅|み} (enchant/charm) instead of the standard {見|み} of {見|み}せる (to show). This spelling emphasizes the captivating or spellbinding quality of what is being shown.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {観客|かんきゃく}を{魅|み}せる (captivate the audience)
- {演技|えんぎ}で{魅|み}せる (enchant with a performance)
- {魅|み}せるプレー (a dazzling play/performance)

USAGE NOTES:
Often appears in entertainment, sports, and arts contexts. The passive form {魅|み}せられる (to be captivated) is also common. Related to {魅了|みりょう}する (to fascinate) and {魅力|みりょく} (charm/appeal), all sharing the kanji {魅|み}. In casual writing, sometimes used interchangeably with {見|み}せる to add dramatic flair, but the distinction is meaningful in careful writing.
